title: Authentication Using External IDP
body:
Hi team,

I'm wondering how to achieve authentication in MLflow using an external IDP via OIDC/OAuth. Are there any existing plugins that supports this? And is this even feasible via a custom authentication plugin?

Additionally, once authentication is enabled, are we still able to manage existing permissions? As far as I know, the permissions are stored in basic_auth.db and there is no way to define/manage these outside of a standard database.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: We're looking into supporting OAuth2 in this quarter. Please stay tuned! Right now it's not possible to do what you're trying to do.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: Regarding OIDC/Oauth, you can easily achieve that by using oauth2-proxy as a sidecar pattern if you are serving a container-based tracking server. Here is my demo code https://github.com/cloudacode/mlflow-oauth-sidecar

comments.author: participant9
comments.body:
Hi everyone! There is already a nice third party plugin which implements several features at https://github.com/data-platform-hq/mlflow-oidc-auth

Features:
- API authentication based on OIDC token as well as long term API token
- Role based authorization for models and experiments  
- Control which user is allowed to use MlFlow based on the existence of a custom field in the OIDC token
- User registration via OIDC login 

We are happy to discuss any feedback or to make a PR.

Please react to this comment in case this might be interesting for the community!
(@participant7 @participant3 , @participant14 , @participant6, @participant4 , @reporter, @participant1 )

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
> @participant7 May I ask how did you handle auth over MLflow SDK (the python API) with oauth2-proxy? I knew it's a good tool for browser traffic, but had hard time dealing with the SDK.

You only need to set the TOKEN to the `MLFLOW_TRACKING_TOKEN` environment value. then MLflow SDK will request authentication through oauth2-proxy with the TOKEN. If you have a separate OAuth client for generating tokens for your machine, you can add that client as an extra-jwt-issuers in oauth2-proxy config.

You can find my completed example in my previous comment above.

comments.author: participant7
comments.body: @participant4 Yes, after comparing options, I ended up using 'htpasswd' option for SDK access. Then you will need to configure `MLFLOW_TRACKING_PASSWORD` and `MLFLOW_TRACKING_USERNAME` to use the basic authentication. Otherwise you will need to create jwt and handle token refresh. You may take a look at [AuthLib](https://<redacted-host>/en/latest/).

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
@participant4 May I ask how your other apps programmatically fetch the token? Essentially, OAuth2-Proxy simply relays the authentication request—more precisely, it retrieves the JSON Web Key from the IdP and verifies the JWT—rather than generating the token itself. If your IdP offers an SDK or CLI to fetch the token, you can use that to obtain the token and set it as an env variable to access MLflow over OAuth2-Proxy.

For example, if Google is your external IdP, you can use the Google SDK to fetch the token and programmatically pass it to your MLflow tracking code.
